facts.statement: Wahasuchus lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Campanian,

facts.statement: The genus Wahasuchus was first described in 2018.
facts.quote: First described in 2018

facts.statement: Fossils of Wahasuchus have been found in the Quseir Formation in Egypt.
facts.quote: found in the Quseir Formation, Egypt

facts.statement: The fossils of Wahasuchus were discovered in 2010 by researchers from Mansoura University.
facts.quote: with the discovery having been made in 2010 by members of Mansoura University

facts.statement: All known material was collected from an outcrop near Mut in the Dakhla Oasis of Egypt's Western Desert.
facts.quote: All material assigned to this taxon have been collected form an outcrop near Mut in Dakhla Oasis in Egypts Western Desert

facts.statement: Sara Saber and colleagues formally described the material in 2018.
facts.quote: The material was described by Sara Saber and colleagues in 2018

facts.statement: The fossils are currently held in the collection of the Mansoura University Vertebrate Paleontology Center.
facts.quote: and is held in the collection of the Mansoura University Vertebrate Paleontology Center

facts.statement: Besides the holotype skull remains, additional fossils from a nearby bonebed were assigned to the genus.
facts.quote: In addition to the various skull remains that form the holotype, several additional fossils were referred to Wahasuchus from a nearby bonebed

facts.statement: Wahasuchus is classified as an extinct mesoeucrocodylian and is likely a member of the Neosuchia clade.
facts.quote: Wahasuchus is an extinct genus of engimatic mesoeucrocodylian, likely a neosuchian

facts.statement: The genus Wahasuchus currently contains only one species, Wahasuchus egyptensis.
facts.quote: The genus currently only contains a single species, Wahasuchus egyptensis

facts.statement: The genus is known primarily from fragmentary remains that represent multiple individuals.
facts.quote: known mostly from fragmentary remains representing multiple individuals

facts.statement: The skull's generally flattened morphology, similar to modern crocodiles, suggests it belonged to the Neosuchia clade.
facts.quote: features of the skull including its generally flattened morphology akin to that of modern crocodiles suggests it was part of the clade Neosuchia

facts.statement: Reassembly of available parts suggests the skull was platyrostral, or flattened like that of modern crocodiles.
facts.quote: reassembly based on what is available suggests that the skull of Wahasuchus was platyrostral, meaning it was flattened in a similar manner to those of modern crocodiles

facts.statement: The snout was massively built with expanded individual elements that gave the rostrum significant depth.
facts.quote: the snout of Wahasuchus was massively built, with the individual elements being relatively expanded giving some depth to the rostrum

facts.statement: There were five alveoli (tooth sockets) in each premaxilla bone.
facts.quote: Five alveoli were present in each premaxilla

facts.statement: The maxilla contained 14 teeth.
facts.quote: of which there are 14

facts.statement: The first wave of tooth enlargement involved the first five teeth, peaking in size at the third maxillary tooth.
facts.quote: The first wave of tooth enlargement consists of the first five teeth, gradually becoming larger until they hit their peak with the third maxillary tooth

facts.statement: The second wave of tooth enlargement spanned from the sixth to the fourteenth tooth.
facts.quote: The second wave of tooth enlargement spans from the sixth to fourteenth tooth

facts.statement: The last seven maxillary teeth were confluent, with little to no space between their sockets.
facts.quote: the last seven being confluent, with little to no space between the individual tooth sockets

facts.statement: The anterior process of the jugal bone was especially large, being three times as broad as the posterior process.
facts.quote: The anterior process in Wahasuchus is especially large, thrice as broad as the posterior process

facts.statement: The ventral surface of the jugal bore foramina and pits, while the surface below the eyesockets was marked by shallow grooves.
facts.quote: the ventral surface bearing foramina and pits and the surface just below the eyesockets being marked by shallow grooves

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesize that the quadrate bones had no contact with the exoccipital bone, though they note this might be due to preservation issues.
facts.quote: Saber and colleagues hypothesize that there was no contact with the exoccipital bone, unlike in goniopholidids and allodaposuchids, though they mention that this might also be caused by preservation

facts.statement: The postorbital bone of Wahasuchus has a triradiate structure with three main sections.
facts.quote: The postorbital is triradiate, meaning it consists of three main sections.

facts.statement: The dentary of Wahasuchus contained at least 16 teeth, with preservation suggesting a total of 17 or 18 teeth.
facts.quote: At least 16 teeth were housed in the dentary, although preservation suggests that one or two more were likely present, bringing the total to 17 or 18 teeth.

facts.statement: The fourth tooth in the lower jaw of Wahasuchus is the largest and fits into a notch between the upper premaxillary and maxillary teeth.
facts.quote: As is most often the case for neosuchians, the largest tooth of the lower jaw is the fourth, which slides neatly into the notch present between the premaxillary and maxillary teeth in the upper jaw.

facts.statement: Features like a flattened skull, enclosed otic opening, and simple dentition suggest Wahasuchus belongs to the group Neosuchia.
facts.quote: Some features would agree with Wahasuchus being classified as a member of neosuchia, such as the flattened skull, enclosed otic opening and the simple dentition.

facts.statement: The amphicoelous nature of Wahasuchus vertebrae suggests it may be an early-diverging member of Neosuchia.
facts.quote: The fact that the vertebrae are amphicoelous suggests that it could have been an early-diverging member of the group

facts.statement: Wahasuchus lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Wahasuchus is Wahasuchus egyptensis.
facts.quote: Type species: Wahasuchus egyptensis

facts.statement: Wahasuchus likely spent much of its time in water and had an opportunistic diet that included turtles, fish, and land vertebrates.
facts.quote: This suggests that it likely spend much of its time in the water and had opportunistic feeding preferences, its prey possibly including turtles, fish and various land vertebrates.

facts.statement: The platyrostral snout shape of Wahasuchus was likely acquired convergently, similar to many other neosuchians and modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: The generalized platyrostral snout shape, which Wahasuchus shares with a great many neosuchians including most modern crocodilians, was likely acquired convergently to these animals

facts.statement: The exact relationship of Wahasuchus with other crocodyliforms remains elusive due to poor fossil preservation, particularly of the palate.
facts.quote: This does however also mean that its exact relationship with other crocodyliforms remains elusive, not helped by the poor preservation of the known material, especially concerning the palate.
